office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Open seat left by Rep. Mike Volz, now Spokane County treasurer. Democrat Michaela Kelso, a retired Army linguist who led the six-way primary, faces Republican Alan Nolan, a Mead School Board director and retired Air Force officer; they split on the tax on income over $1 million, I-1 and I-638, housing regulation and data centers.

candidates.summary: Retired U.S. Army intelligence linguist and Democratic party officer, on her third run for the Legislature, whose priorities are housing costs, health care and school funding.
highlights: Supports the 2026 tax on income over $1 million: "Let them pay their fair share" [S2]
Favors density, affordable units inside market-rate projects and rent-control legislation [S5][S6]
Wants a temporary statewide moratorium on data centers [S2]

taxes.basis: Supports the tax on income over $1 million and says higher earners should be taxed at a higher rate.

spending.basis: Calls for guaranteeing and funding quality education and lowering the school-bond threshold so districts need not 'beg' for funds.

housing.basis: Backed rent-control legislation and wants inclusionary affordable units, alongside upzoning away from single-family-only land.

healthcare.basis: Calls single-payer systems 'vastly superior' but proposes incremental regulation of insurers and drug costs as the starting point.

social.basis: Opposes I-638 (objecting to its sex-verification requirement); endorsed by Planned Parenthood Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Opposes I-1 and says educators, not outside mandates, should determine what students learn.

tech.basis: Favors a temporary statewide data-center moratorium until the Legislature sets rules.

experience.basis: Has never held public office (party PCO and state committee member only); opponent holds a school-board seat.

candidates.summary: Mead School Board director since 2023, retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and co-owner of a design and construction firm, running on spending cuts, lower taxes and school choice.
highlights: Opposes the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and campaigned against a transit sales-tax renewal [S2][S7]
Top goal is restoring fiscal responsibility through spending reductions [S8]
Supports I-638 and state education dollars following students to charter and private schools [S7][S2]
Would revert the state energy code to 2018 and reform the Growth Management Act to lower housing costs [S2][S8]

taxes.basis: Opposes the tax on income over $1 million ('We do not need another tax') and campaigned against renewing STA's sales tax.

spending.basis: Top goal is spending reductions; pledges agency performance results and named a 50% cut to the attorney general's budget.

housing.basis: Would lower housing costs by repealing energy-code mandates, loosening GMA land restrictions and cutting fees and regulations.

climate.basis: Wants recent energy-efficiency building mandates repealed, saying the state limits energy use without regard to cost.

local-control.basis: Says local governments should decide data-center locations: 'I believe in local control.'

tech.basis: Says Eastern Washington has good reasons to host data centers, subject to a robust local process; no moratorium.

social.basis: Asks voters to approve I-638 and worked with school directors statewide on girls'-sports proposals.

parental-rights.basis: Calls parents the 'rightful authority' over their children's education and backs funding that follows the student and school choice.

experience.basis: School-board director since 2023 with state building-code roles; no legislative tenure.
